Can you make your code’s hash equal 0?

This pretend lock compares hashes, so it can accept the wrong passcode.

What is a collision?

A hash is a short result made from an input using a rule. A collision happens when different inputs make the same hash.

Our rule has only 10 possible results: 0 to 9. There are 10,000 four-digit codes, including codes starting with 0. Lots of codes must share a hash!

Your discoveries 0

Try a code to see your results here. Find three different codes that open the lock!

    Explore together · parent & child

    First: try 1234. It opens the lock, but it is the original code, so this is not a collision. Next: try 4321. Different code, same hash! Then: try 5555. Its total is 20, and its hash is also 0. Can Orion explain why?

    Try 1235 too: its hash is 1, so it stays locked. Ask: “Does knowing the hash tell you the original passcode?”

    This is a deliberately weak teaching hash. Strong cryptographic hashes have many more possible results and are designed to make finding collisions extremely difficult. This toy rule must not be used to protect real passwords.
